results.evidence: Neither stored figure looks right. The USGS ground height of the two lake surfaces (located from the mapped Ice Lakes outlines) is ~7,173 ft for Upper Ice Lake and ~6,807 ft for Lower Ice Lake, and ~7,618 ft at the mapped Freezer Pass saddle; this agrees with a published statement that the upper lake sits roughly 400 ft above the lower, with another route's camp list giving Ice Lakes at 7,173 ft, and with a hike listing whose high point at Lower Ice Lake is ~6,900 ft. So the drop to Lower Ice Lake is ~800 ft (not 1,000) and waypoints[4].elev 6,600 is ~200 ft low, but any replacement drop figure would be a subtraction of two heights rather than a stated number, and the ~500 ft line may refer to the upper basin. Left unresolved with these measurements.
